description: The USING phrase of the ASSIGN clause (ISO §2023:12.4.5.3 GR3 b) / §2023:9.1.21 dynamic file assignment: the file connector is associated with the physical file named by data-name-1's content at each OPEN, SORT or MERGE), on BOTH arms of the clause - `ASSIGN TO {device-name-1 | literal-1}... USING data-name-1` and the bare `ASSIGN USING data-name-1`. A COBOL-2002 introduction. THE EDGE IS DERIVED, NOT QUOTED (the repo holds no 2002 or 2014 text, ratified decision #1; the R61 method): Annex E, which itemizes the 2014->2023 delta, never names the phrase, so it predates 2023; GnuCOBOL's per-standard dialect files date it at 2002 - cobol85.conf `assign-using-variable: unconformable`, cobol2002.conf and cobol2014.conf `ok` - and cobc 3.2 -std=cobol85 refuses `SELECT F ASSIGN USING WS-NAME` ('ASSIGN USING/VARYING variable does not conform to COBOL 85') while -std=cobol2002 accepts it (kb/Work PB746; CLAUDE.md rule 1 precedence: ISO, then GnuCOBOL). Gated in ONE place, the VersionConformancePass parse arm on assignClause (the USING token appears in no other file-control rule).
display: the USING phrase of the ASSIGN clause
citation: ISO §2023:12.4.5.3 GR3 b), §2023:9.1.21; a COBOL-2002 introduction (derived: GnuCOBOL 3.2 cobol85.conf / cobol2002.conf assign-using-variable; VCR row 7.27)
source:
IDENTIFICATION DIVISION.
       PROGRAM-ID. ROWAU.
       ENVIRONMENT DIVISION.
       INPUT-OUTPUT SECTION.
       FILE-CONTROL.
           SELECT F ASSIGN USING WS-NAME ORGANIZATION IS SEQUENTIAL.
       DATA DIVISION.
       FILE SECTION.
       FD F.
       01 R PIC X(8).
       WORKING-STORAGE SECTION.
       01 WS-NAME PIC X(20) VALUE "f.dat".
       PROCEDURE DIVISION.
       MAIN. STOP RUN.
